newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle trade thin at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle trade thin at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets after midday Monday were slow, with light sales noted in Kansas at a top of $72.00 per cwt, steady with last week, feedlot sources said.
About 500 head traded in Kansas, with 400 steers at $72.00 and 100 heifers at $71.00, according to USDA.
There were no sales reported in the Texas Panhandle or western Oklahoma area by USDA or private sources.
Packers were bidding $71.00 to $72.00, mostly $72.00 and owners were pricing cattle from $72.00 to $74.00, with a few at $75.00, cattle feeders said.
Feedlot cattle prices were expected to trade at $73.00 later in the week, lifted by higher boxed beef prices and tight supplies of market-ready cattle.
Showlists this week were estimated near 73,000 head, down 1,500 from a week ago in the Panhandle, and estimated near 54,000 in Kansas, down 1,000 from last week.
Many of the cattle on this week's showlists were said to be extremely 'green' or unfinished.
Beef prices were supported by strong beef clearance during the weekend and light production the past two weeks.
